questions.prompt: To address California's housing crisis, the state should allow more housing to be built near transit stops even if it overrides local zoning rules.
questions.helpText: This is often called 'upzoning' or 'transit-oriented development.' Supporters say it creates homes and reduces sprawl; opponents say it removes local control.

questions.prompt: California should move as fast as possible to phase out gasoline cars and gas appliances, even if it raises costs for residents in the short term.
questions.helpText: California mandates no new gas car sales by 2035. Supporters say this is essential for climate goals; critics say it places undue burden on lower-income households.

questions.prompt: Restoring felony thresholds (as Prop 36 did) and prosecuting more repeat offenders is the most effective path to reducing retail theft and public disorder.
questions.helpText: Prop 36 (2024) raised theft and drug felony thresholds back to pre-Prop 47 levels. Supporters say accountability deters crime; critics say underlying causes need investment.

questions.prompt: California should primarily close its budget deficit by raising taxes on wealthy individuals and corporations rather than cutting services.
questions.helpText: California's recurring deficits require difficult choices. Progressives favor new taxes; conservatives favor spending cuts and growth through deregulation.

questions.prompt: California is right to maintain sanctuary policies that limit local law enforcement cooperation with federal immigration agencies.
questions.helpText: Sanctuary policies prevent local police from informing ICE about undocumented individuals. Supporters say it builds community trust; opponents say it creates public safety risks.

questions.prompt: California should pursue a state-run universal healthcare system (single-payer) that covers all residents regardless of immigration status.
questions.helpText: Single-payer advocates say it's the only way to achieve universal coverage. Critics say the cost would require a massive tax increase and harm current insurance options.

questions.prompt: California needs to significantly increase K-12 teacher pay and classroom funding, even if it requires raising taxes.
questions.helpText: Despite high spending, California's test scores rank near the bottom nationally. Some say more investment is the answer; others say structural reforms matter more.

questions.prompt: Expanding rent control and tenant protections is an important tool to keep long-time residents in their homes.
questions.helpText: Rent control limits rent increases for existing tenants. Supporters say it prevents displacement; economists often argue it reduces housing supply.

questions.prompt: The state should significantly increase funding for forest management and prescribed burns as the primary strategy for wildfire prevention.
questions.helpText: Wildfires have become more destructive. Some favor aggressive fuel management; others prioritize building codes and defensible space requirements.

questions.prompt: California's business regulations and permitting costs are too burdensome and are a leading reason companies are leaving the state.
questions.helpText: California consistently ranks near the bottom for business climate. Some say regulations protect workers and the environment; others say they stifle growth and raise costs.

options.label: Strongly agree — regulations are too burdensome
Somewhat disagree — regulations serve important purposes
Strongly disagree — California should keep strong standards

questions.prompt: California should invest heavily in new water storage (reservoirs, aquifer recharge) to ensure long-term drought resilience.
questions.helpText: Water storage is critical but expensive and environmentally complex. Some favor recycled water and conservation over new infrastructure.

questions.prompt: California should prioritize funding public transit and high-speed rail over expanding roads and highway capacity.
questions.helpText: Transportation spending is a major policy choice. Transit advocates point to climate and equity benefits; roads advocates prioritize practicality in auto-dependent communities.

questions.prompt: Forcing people experiencing homelessness into treatment (conservatorship) against their will is necessary and justified when they are a danger to themselves.
questions.helpText: Prop 1 (2024) restructured mental health funding. CARE Court allows involuntary treatment. Supporters say it saves lives; civil liberties advocates oppose forced care.

questions.prompt: California should continue to provide full state services, including Medi-Cal healthcare, to undocumented immigrants regardless of federal pressure.
questions.helpText: California has expanded Medi-Cal to all income-eligible adults regardless of immigration status, costing billions annually. Supporters cite equity; critics cite cost and federal conflict.

questions.prompt: California should keep its nuclear power plants running (or reopen closed ones) as a low-carbon energy source.
questions.helpText: Diablo Canyon nuclear plant has had its closure reversed. Advocates say nuclear is reliable clean power; opponents cite cost, safety, and waste concerns.

questions.prompt: Charter schools and school choice programs are an important part of improving educational outcomes for California students.
questions.helpText: California has ~1,300 charter schools. Supporters say they provide options for underserved students; critics say they siphon funding from traditional public schools.

questions.prompt: California should use state power to negotiate or cap prescription drug prices for all residents.
questions.helpText: The state AG has sued pharmaceutical companies over pricing. Some want a state formulary with negotiated prices. Industry warns it could reduce innovation and access.

questions.prompt: California should continue investing in the high-speed rail project connecting Los Angeles and San Francisco, despite its cost overruns.
questions.helpText: The project has been over budget and delayed for years. Supporters argue it's essential long-term infrastructure; critics say the money should go to more immediate needs.
